correctness.rationale: A zero coordinate at a projective critical point forces the preceding coordinate to vanish and hence forces all five to vanish. With x_0=1, the first three gradient equations give b=-1/(2a), c=a^3, d=-1/(8a^5) (a is a unit), and the fourth imposes a^11=3 or (a-3)^11=0. The restriction f=5a/8+1/(64a^10) has numerator 40a^11+1 over 64a^10, hence vanishes in the gradient quotient in characteristic 11. This gives the sole support [1:3:9:5:4] and the intrinsic quotient of length 11. The transverse Hessian in a,b,c has determinant 7(80-49)-36*8=-71=6 modulo 11, and d'(3)=5/(8*3^6) is nonzero. Thus d parametrizes the formal transverse critical section. Translating that section to zero leaves a quadratic expression in the transverse variables with invertible symmetric coefficient matrix over the power-series ring; congruence and formal square roots reduce it to three squares, with an invertible transverse linear part. On the section a=3(1+u) gives residual 6(1+u)+5/(1+u)^10=6u^11(1+u)/(1+u^11). Dividing by its unit factor and rescaling the squares proves the complete local ring (contact, not right equivalence). Its Tjurina algebra imposes the three transverse coordinates and u^11; the u derivative vanishes. The supplied checker was inspected, not executed; these exact identities and the formal argument are independent of bounded computations. The published A2 equation would have length 2, not 11.
